## Comparability Caveat

The as-originally-reported FY2022 figure is **not** comparable to FY2024. GE originally reported FY2022 total revenue of $76,555 million [DOC-1], but that figure included two businesses that have since been separated: GE HealthCare (spun off January 3, 2023) and GE Vernova (separated April 2, 2024). Per the FY2024 filing, "Results of both GE HealthCare and GE Vernova are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented in these consolidated financial statements" [DOC-4], and the continuing-operations entity is what is now called GE Aerospace [DOC-4].

This restatement is visible in the successive filings: FY2022 revenue was shown as $76,555M in the FY2022 10-K [DOC-1], then $58,100M in the FY2023 10-K (post-HealthCare) [DOC-2], and finally $29,139M in the FY2024 10-K (post-Vernova) [DOC-3]. Comparing $38,702M to $76,555M would produce a meaningless ~(49)% decline driven entirely by divestitures, not operating performance.

## Like-for-Like Calculation

Using the consistently restated continuing-operations (GE Aerospace) basis from the FY2024 10-K:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| FY2024 total revenue [DOC-3] | $38,702M |
| FY2022 total revenue, as recast in FY2024 10-K [DOC-3] | $29,139M |
| Change | +$9,563M |
| Growth | +32.8% |

$9,563M ÷ $29,139M = **32.8%** over two years, implying a CAGR of roughly 15.2%.

ANSWER: +32.8% (from $29,139M in FY2022 to $38,702M in FY2024, both on the restated GE Aerospace continuing-operations basis; the originally reported FY2022 revenue of $76,555M is not comparable due to the GE HealthCare and GE Vernova separations)
